nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-03.title: Angle chasing
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-03.body:
Let $m\angle BAC=4x$, so $m\angle BAD=m\angle DAC=2x$ and $m\angle DAE=m\angle EAC=x$. Let $m\angle ABC=5y$, $m\angle AEB=2y$, $m\angle ACB=y$.

$\angle AEB$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle AEC$, so $2y=x+y$, giving $x=y$. The angles of $\triangle ABC$ give $4x+5y+y=180^\circ$, so $x=y=18^\circ$.

In $\triangle ADC$: $m\angle ADC=180^\circ-2x-y=180^\circ-54^\circ=126^\circ$.

In $\triangle AEC$: $m\angle AEC=180^\circ-x-y=144^\circ$.

Sum: $126^\circ+144^\circ=270^\circ$.

**Answer: 270**

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-04.title: Factor cleverly
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-04.body: Let $a=2013$. First factor: $(a^2+1)(a^4-a^2+1)=a^6+1$ (multiply out or use the identity). Second factor: $(a^2-1)(a^2+a+1)(a^2-a+1)=(a^2-1)(a^4+a^2+1)=a^6-1$. So the expression is $(a^6+1)-(a^6-1)=2$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-06.title: Substitute y=x-1
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-06.body: Let $y=x-1$, $x=y+1$. Expanding $(y+1)^3-4(y+1)^2+7(y+1)-6=y^3-y^2+2y-2$. By Vieta's on the new polynomial: $\sum 1/y_i = (\text{sum of products of pairs})/(\text{product})=2/2=1$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-07.title: Divide out 7!
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-07.body: $A!\cdot B!=10!/7!=8\cdot9\cdot10=720$. Try factorizations: $3!\cdot5!=6\cdot120=720$. ✓ So $(A,B)=(3,5)$ or $(5,3)$, giving $A+B=8$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-10.title: Count favorable arrangements
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-10.body: Total: $\binom{12}{3}=220$. Horizontal (3 consecutive in a row of 4): 2 sets per row $\times$ 3 rows = 6. Vertical (3 in a column of 3): 4 columns = 4. Diagonal: 2 going right-down + 2 going left-down = 4. Total favorable = 6+4+4=14. $P=14/220=7/110$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-12.title: Angle bisector condition
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-12.body: The angle bisector between lines with slopes 1 and 2 has slope $m$ satisfying $\left|\frac{1-m}{1+m}\right|=\left|\frac{2-m}{1+2m}\right|$. Taking the case that gives a slope between 1 and 2: $3m^2-2m-3=0$, $m=\frac{2+\sqrt{40}}{6}=\frac{1+\sqrt{10}}{3}$. So $(a,b,c)=(1,10,3)$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-17.title: Pappus's theorem
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-17.body: Place $RA$ on the $y$-axis: $A=(0,0)$, $R=(0,6)$. Since $TP\parallel RA$, $T$ and $P$ share an $x$-coordinate $d$. From $AP=13$: $d^2+p_y^2=169$; $TR=15$: $d^2+(t_y-6)^2=225$; $TP=20$: $t_y-p_y=20$. Solving: $p_y=-5$, $t_y=15$, $d=12$. Area of trapezoid: $\frac{1}{2}(6+20)\cdot12=156$. Centroid distance from axis: $\bar{x}=\frac{d}{3}\cdot\frac{a+2b}{a+b}=\frac{12}{3}\cdot\frac{6+40}{26}=\frac{92}{13}$. Volume: $2\pi\bar{x}\cdot A=2\pi\cdot\frac{92}{13}\cdot156=2208\pi$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-18.title: Count crossings period by period
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-18.body:
Here $\log$ is base $10$. Since $|2\cos x|\le2$, solutions need $-2\le\log x\le2$, i.e. $0.01\le x\le100$.

On $(0,2\pi]$, $\log x<0.8$ while $2\cos x$ falls from $2$ to $-2$ and rises back to $2$, so the graphs cross twice (once on the downswing, once on the upswing). The same happens on each interval $[2k\pi,2(k+1)\pi]$ for $k=0,1,\dots,14$, since $\log x<2$ there ($30\pi\approx94.2<100$). That gives $2\cdot15=30$ intersections.

On $[30\pi,100]$, $2\cos x$ starts at $2>\log x$ and decreases, giving one more crossing; it does not climb back above $\log x$ before $x=100$ (the next peak is at $32\pi>100$, where $\log x>2$ anyway).

Total: $30+1=31$.

**Answer: 31**

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-21.title: Find integer solutions
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-21.body:
We need integers $m=\lfloor x\rfloor$, $n=\lfloor y\rfloor$ with $m^2+n^2=2$, so $(m,n)=(\pm1,\pm1)$: four pairs. Each pair gives the unit square $m\le x<m+1$, $n\le y<n+1$. The total area is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-23.title: Law of sines
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-23.body: $\sin T=3/5$, $\cos T=4/5$; $\sin N=15/17$, $\cos N=8/17$. $\sin A=\sin(T+N)=\sin T\cos N+\cos T\sin N=\frac{24}{85}+\frac{60}{85}=\frac{84}{85}$. By law of sines: $\frac{TA}{\sin N}=\frac{TN}{\sin A}$, so $\frac{TA}{TN}=\frac{\sin N}{\sin A}=\frac{15/17}{84/85}=\frac{75}{84}=\frac{25}{28}$.

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-24.title: Stars and bars
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-24.body:
Write $12$ as a row of $12$ ones; a twelvey triple corresponds to placing $2$ dividers in the $11$ gaps between them (each part must be nonempty). The count is $\binom{11}{2}=55$.

**Answer: 55**

nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-27.title: Largest and smallest
nyciml-2013-14-fall-seniorb-27.body: Greatest 3-digit base-8 number: $777_8=7\cdot64+7\cdot8+7=511$. Least 3-digit base-12 number: $100_{12}=144$. $F+L=511+144=655$.
